name: bind_re_match
title: Match a data frame column and attach the results

origin.description: Runs re_match on a column and attaches the new columns. The R argument from is column, because from is a Python keyword.
origin.details: Runs re_match on a column and attaches the new columns. The R argument from is column, because from is a Python keyword.
origin.value: bind_re_match of Mazda RX4 returns make Mazda and model RX4.
origin.example:
cars <- data.frame(rowname = "Mazda RX4", mpg = 21, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bind_re_match_(cars, "rowname", "^(?<make>\\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$")

translation.description: Runs re_match on a column and attaches the new columns. The R argument from is column, because from is a Python keyword.
translation.details: Runs re_match on a column and attaches the new columns. The R argument from is column, because from is a Python keyword.
translation.value: bind_re_match of Mazda RX4 returns make Mazda and model RX4.
translation.example:
from rematch2 import bind_re_match
from tibble import tibble
cars = tibble(rowname=["Mazda RX4"], mpg=[21.0])
print(bind_re_match(cars, "rowname", r"^(?<make>\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$")["make"])
